thread:
deploy-bot: Deployment event: sdk-paging v6 -> canary (10%) started at 2026-03-15T09:01Z. Monitoring hooks enabled.

deploy-bot: ALERT: spike in 5xx on /v1/stream/paging (rolling 5m). error_rate=8% (baseline 0.3%), p95 latency up 3x.

anya: @channel customer reports coming in — streaming paging sessions failing to complete handshake, repeated reconnect loops.

mike: Checked logs on canary nodes, looks like a proto/frame mismatch. Sample from node-usw2-a: 
```
ERROR[03-15T09:03:22Z] stream-handshake failed client_id=abc123 err="unexpected frame tag: 0x03 != expected 0x02" stack=...
```

jess: Canary is at 10% applied to us-west-2 pools (a/b). Which runtime was in the build? Anyone changed header encoding?

lucas: I pushed the runtime bump — included a small refactor that renamed header field and bumped frame version. Looks like clients still expect old frame tag. My bad.

anya: Ok immediate mitigation: flip feature flag to force streaming fallback to polling path for SDKs while we investigate. Flag: `streaming_v6_enable` -> false. Who can flip now?

mike: I can. Flipping now: `fflip set streaming_v6_enable false --env prod --reason \"proto mismatch\"`

deploy-bot: Feature flag change accepted. Propagating to edge ~30s.

emily: Confirming traffic shift — clients are falling back to /v1/poll/paging. Error spike dropping, current error_rate=0.9% (2m). UX degraded but sessions continue.

mike: Kicking canary rollback to be safe: `release-cli rollback --id sdk-paging-v6 --to sdk-paging-v5 --reason \"proto incompatibility with deployed clients\"`

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated. Reverting canary nodes... 6/6 nodes reverted.

jess: Can we run quick acceptance and replay tests against reverted nodes to ensure idempotency?

lucas: Running integration suite now. Looks green on handshakes and reconnection behaviour. I also spotted a duplicate event window on reconnect for one path — small edge case.

anya: Noted. Customer impact: identified 12 active customers that hit the failing path; most auto-fell back to polling after FF flip. Opening support tickets for the ones with duplicate events.

incident-bot: Incident created INC-20260315-42 — severity: high — owners: mike, anya — timeline pinned to this thread.

anya: Handoff: I'm going offline in 10m, handing on-call to @mike at 11:00 UTC. Summary for handoff: FF flipped to disable streaming v6, canary rolled back to v5, acceptance tests passing, watch for replays/duplicates and any slow polling degradation.

mike: Taking handoff. Next steps: patch runtime to accept both frame tags (compat shim), add decoder integration tests, and include a canary gating test for header versioning. Planning hotfix release with compatibility flag — ETA ~4h. I'll draft the postmortem and customer comms.

emily: Quick customer impact note: top 3 accounts experienced UX stutter for ~5–10 minutes; no data corruption found aside from duplicate event window for one account which Support is handling.

anya: TL;DR root cause — protocol field rename in runtime release caused streaming clients to mismatch frame tag. Mitigation — FF kill -> polling fallback, rollback canary. Action items — compatibility patch, stronger canary tests, add explicit schema/decoder check in CI.

mike: I'll create INC follow-up playbook items and a PR with the compatibility shim. Updating stakeholders and scheduling postmortem review.

jess: Leaving notes for SRE runbook: add alert for sudden protocol-version drift (frame mismatch errors) and a quickplay to flip streaming FF and trigger rollback.

anaya: thanks all — keeping thread pinned.
